div.head: Leis Wl 52.1
div.ab: E si il s'ent fuist dedenz la chalange, li sire rende sun were.
Quodsi infra rectacionem aliquis fugerit, dominus soluat were.
E si il s'ent fuist dedenz la chalange, li sire rende sun were.
52, 1. Wenn jener jedoch während des Anklagezustandes entflieht, zahle der Herr dessen Wergeld.
52, 1. If, however, that man flees while under accusation, the lord shall pay his wergild.
And if he escapes while he is under the accusation, the lord shall pay his wergeld.
div.note: Added October 2026 from Robertson pp. 274–275 (text and translation); Liebermann’s text and German translation added from Gesetze I p. 520, October 2026 (two independent readings of the page images)

note.seg: L meint wahrscheinlich und I vielleicht Wergeld des Herrn, gegen meine Übs. Diese Abweichung von Cnut scheint absichtlich, weil 52, 2, wo Cnut dieses höhere Wergeld anordnet, es fortgelassen ist. Vgl. o. S. 148 zu I Atr 1, 13{1}

L probably means, and I perhaps, the lord’s wergild, contrary to my translation. This departure from Cnut seems deliberate, because in 52, 2, where Cnut prescribes this higher wergild, it has been left out. Cf. above p. 148 on I Atr 1, 13{1}
